sc01: During conversations, I often have to consciously work out when it is my turn to speak.
sc02: I usually notice naturally when another person wants to change the subject.
sc03: When someone tells me about their day, I usually know what kind of response they expect without analysing it.
sc04: Back-and-forth conversation can feel like a process I have to consciously manage.
sc05: I sometimes keep explaining something that interests me after the other person has lost interest.
sc06: Spontaneous conversations generally feel easier to me than conversations I have prepared for.
sc07: When someone’s words, facial expression and tone do not match, I can be unsure which signal to trust.
sc08: I usually recognise from tone and facial expression when someone is joking.
sc09: Managing eye contact can require conscious effort or make it harder for me to think.
sc10: My facial expressions or gestures do not always happen automatically at the moments other people seem to expect.
sc11: I usually notice subtle signs that another person is becoming bored or irritated.
sc12: In group conversations, it can be difficult to track who is expected to speak next.
sc13: It can be unclear to me how an acquaintance is supposed to become a close friend.
sc14: I consciously change how I behave depending on the social setting.
sc15: I can usually maintain friendships without consciously keeping track of social rules.
sc16: After social situations, I often review what I said or did to check whether I handled them correctly.
sc17: Unstructured social gatherings are harder for me than interactions with a clear purpose.
sc18: Unspoken social hierarchies and alliances usually make intuitive sense to me.
rrb01: When I am excited, stressed or absorbed, I repeat small movements, sounds, words or actions.
rrb02: I sometimes use or arrange objects in a preferred repeated way even when there is no practical need.
rrb03: Repeating familiar music, videos, passages, games or activities can help me regulate myself.
rrb04: I have repetitive movements or habits that I consciously suppress around other people.
same01: An unexpected change to my planned day can cost me much more energy than the change itself seems to justify.
same02: Before an unfamiliar event, I strongly prefer knowing the sequence of what will happen.
same03: When priorities change unexpectedly, I can usually switch tasks without much difficulty.
same04: A disrupted routine can affect my concentration or mood long after the change occurred.
same05: I use particular routes, orders or routines because alternatives can feel wrong or unnecessarily demanding.
int01: Some interests absorb me so strongly that I lose track of time or physical needs.
int02: I enjoy collecting unusually detailed information about particular subjects.
int03: It can be difficult to stop researching, discussing or working on an interest even when I intended to do something else.
int04: My interests are generally similar in intensity to those of the people around me.
int05: I can return to the same subject for years and continue wanting to understand it in greater depth.
sen01: Background noises that other people seem to ignore can make it difficult for me to think.
sen02: Bright light, glare or flickering light can be physically exhausting or distracting.
sen03: I notice clothing textures, seams, labels or materials that other people seem not to notice.
sen04: Smells, tastes or food textures strongly influence what environments or foods I can tolerate.
sen05: I sometimes notice hunger, thirst, tiredness or the need to use the toilet only when it has become intense.
sen06: I deliberately seek strong sensory input such as pressure, movement, texture or sound.
sen07: Crowded or sensory-heavy environments can make me shut down, become irritable or need to leave.
sen08: I can usually filter out irrelevant sensory information without much effort.
sen09: My reactions to pain or temperature sometimes seem noticeably different from those of people around me.
sen10: After sensory overload, I often need quiet or time alone before I feel normal again.
dev01: Joining group activities or conversations without an explicit invitation was difficult for me.
dev02: Predictable routines or rituals were unusually important to me.
dev03: I had interests that were unusually intense or detailed.
dev04: Sounds, clothing, food, light or other sensory experiences affected me strongly.
dev05: Indirect language, hints or implied meanings were easy for me to misunderstand.
dev06: I often preferred solitary activities or interacting outside my own peer group.
dev07: I copied, rehearsed or consciously learned ways of behaving socially.
dev08: Unexpected changes could upset me much more than other people seemed to expect.
dev09: I repeatedly made particular movements, sounds or actions when excited, stressed or absorbed.
dev10: Knowing when and how to enter a conversation was difficult.
dev11: Social demands could leave me unusually tired afterwards.
dev12: I often felt different from other people without clearly understanding why.
mask01: Before social situations, I rehearse possible sentences or conversations in my head.
mask02: I have learned social expressions, gestures or phrases partly by observing and copying other people.
mask03: I consciously control eye contact, facial expression or body language so that I appear socially appropriate.
mask04: I hide sensory discomfort so other people do not notice how strongly something affects me.
mask05: I use prepared scripts for common situations such as greetings, phone calls or small talk.
mask06: During social interaction, I sometimes monitor myself as though I were watching myself from the outside.
mask07: Social situations often look easier for me from the outside than they feel internally.
mask08: After spending a long time behaving in socially expected ways, I need time to recover.
mask09: I suppress movements, behaviours or reactions in public that I allow myself when alone.
mask10: Without deliberate social strategies, other people would probably notice a clear difference in how I interact.
impact01: Social demands interfere with my work, studies or other responsibilities.
impact02: Unexpected changes or uncertainty interfere with my ability to function.
impact03: Sensory difficulties restrict places, clothing, foods, activities or transport I can comfortably use.
impact04: Maintaining relationships requires an amount of energy that is difficult to sustain.
impact05: Recovery after social or sensory demands reduces the time I have for other parts of my life.
impact06: Misunderstandings in communication repeatedly create conflict or practical problems.
impact07: My routines or intense interests sometimes make ordinary responsibilities harder to manage.
impact08: Overall, these patterns cause meaningful difficulty or distress in my everyday life.
adhd01: My attention frequently moves away from what I intended to focus on.
adhd02: I often begin another task before finishing the one I was already doing.
adhd03: I regularly lose track of objects, appointments or obligations even when I try to organise them.
adhd04: I sometimes speak or act before I have had time to consider the consequences.
adhd05: I frequently need movement, novelty or stimulation to stay engaged.
adhd06: My difficulties change strongly depending on boredom, novelty or reward.
anx01: I usually understand what is socially expected but worry that I will be judged negatively.
anx02: My social difficulties become much smaller when I feel completely safe with the people involved.
anx03: I avoid social situations mainly because I fear embarrassment or rejection.
anx04: Before social situations, I often experience strong physical anxiety.
anx05: When I replay conversations afterwards, my main concern is that other people judged me negatively.
anx06: If I knew nobody could judge me, most social rules would make sense to me.
ocd01: I repeat actions mainly to prevent something bad from happening.
ocd02: Unwanted intrusive thoughts drive some of my repeated behaviours.
ocd03: Some repeated behaviours feel unwanted rather than comforting or naturally preferable.
ocd04: Resisting a ritual can make me afraid that a specific harmful consequence will occur.
ocd05: My routines are sometimes linked to a specific feared consequence rather than simply a preference for predictability.
dep01: My social difficulties mainly appeared or became much stronger during periods of low mood.
dep02: During low periods, I lose interest even in subjects that normally absorb me.
dep03: Low energy or motivation can make social interaction difficult even when I understand what is expected.
dep04: My current social pattern is substantially different from how I functioned before periods of depression or burnout.
dep05: When my mood improves, my social or sensory difficulties also become much smaller.
quality01: I can usually tell when someone means something different from the literal words they are saying.
quality02: Last-minute changes usually require little adjustment from me.
quality03: I can normally ignore background sounds when I need to concentrate.
quality04: I rarely think in advance about what I should say in ordinary social interactions.
quality05: For this item only, please choose ‘Sometimes’.
quality06: For this item only, please choose ‘Rarely’.
